doc.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006

title: The musicians' union, non-union gigs and being busted
summary: Most of his gigs were with half non-union bands; he was called before the board, and teaching pay was poor, but union dinner gigs paid bills.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Did the musician’s union have much to do with the day-to-day music that was going on in New Orleans during your career?

Yeah they had something to do with it, yeah. They had something to do. But I mean there is just so much that they were doing. If you wanted to make some money I mean you had to do what they could provide for you and then do other things too you know. So it was like being non-musicians. Like most gigs I played coming up man, I played with a band that more than half of the band were not in the union, but it was fun, we were making gigs and making money. One time I got busted for playing with the guys and I had to go before the board. But I don’t know it was crazy man. I wanted to say well what do you expect man, I’ve got a family, at the time I had two kids, I have three altogether. I said I need money, I’ve got to work. And you know teaching school in New Orleans, that’s poverty level you know, it’s a shame, it’s a damn shame, schools. I can say that on tape — you might have to bleep that out. But and then I was having fun because mostly my

comrades I was playing with — I used to do some union gig with the bow tie and all that, and you’re playing dinner engagements or stuff like that man. That was cool. That helped pay the bills. It helped me to do what I wanted to do later on in my life and not do the type of gigs that — I don’t have to play music right now if I don’t want to because, like I say, I’m retired from teaching so I don’t have to get out there and bust the pavement trying to do gigs man. And I’m more selective now in what I play because I just don’t have to be out there. And it doesn’t feed what I need to right now because the scene has changed so much. When I play now I want to really get full enjoyment out of what I do. I don’t have to do a gig and me watching my watch, man when is this over with. I hate that man.
Yeah. It seems like the time is standing still.
